### Your GTNH Discord Username

PlayfulPiano

### Your Pack Version

N/A

### Your Server

N/A

### Java Version

Other versions in between

### Type of Server

None

### Your Expectation

When creating an issue within the Github Mobile App, templates would be generated after picking one.

### The Reality

As shown in the below image, every template button instead leads to an external link, which in turn causes a browser "pick an app" loop that never actually reaches the template. Because of this, it is literally impossible to create any issue inside the main modpack repo on the mobile app.
![db9dd3c627c0a65ec5425c64ee1686cb0d73b9915806a073ac0f7f53ba4216db](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b605f131-f0d2-4587-b510-89af653cb3a7)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e6eade6-d6ce-4232-8bd4-14de8df666c4)


### Your Proposal

This is probably a GitHub App limitation, but at least for the time being, it might be worthwhile to keep a blank issue option available for mobile app users. The NotEnoughItems repo has this option available for reference which does work for mobile app users:
![e634c2125ea1e821c9437691e05945f7cc892d3cc8c980a4a62b077b3b5e86b0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49d363fb-a907-41ff-a8e4-fe45708bf1c1)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19db4557-df8d-4458-978a-2823f7d52d0d)

It will scan repositories for package manager files (e.g. from npm/Yarn, Bundler, Composer, Go Modules, Pip/Pipenv/Poetry, Maven/Gradle, Dockerfile/k8s, and many more), and submit Pull Requests with updated versions whenever they are found.

### Intelligent, helpful onboarding

![Onboarding](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/onboarding.png)

```json
{

  "ignorePaths": ["examples/**"],
  "packageRules": [{

}
```

### Support for monorepo directory structures

Renovate will scan all files in each repository to look for relevant package files. It will also group upgrades from the same monorepo into a single PR to ensure tests pass and PR noise is reduced. Natively supports Lerna and Yarn Workspaces with zero configuration necessary.

platform/x86: hp-wmi: mark 8A15 board for timed OMEN thermal profile

The HP OMEN 8 (2022), corresponding to a board ID of 8A15, supports OMEN
thermal profile and requires the timed profile quirk.

Upon adding this ID to both the omen_thermal_profile_boards and
omen_timed_thermal_profile_boards, significant bump in performance can be
observed. For instance, SilverBench (https://silver.urih.com/) results
improved from ~56,000 to ~69,000, as a result of higher power draws (and
thus core frequencies) whilst under load:

Package Power:

- Before the patch: ~65W (dropping to about 55W under sustained load).
- After the patch: ~115W (dropping to about 105W under sustained load).

Core Power:

- Before: ~60W (ditto above).
- After: ~108W (ditto above).

Add 8A15 to omen_thermal_profile_boards and
omen_timed_thermal_profile_boards to improve performance.

issue.body:
# **Feature Request: Lips Movement Detection Model**

---

### **Is your feature request related to a specific feature or functionality? Please describe.**  
I want to request the design and implementation of a **Lips Movement Detection Model**. This feature would allow real-time tracking and analysis of lips movement, which can be integrated into main proctoring system

---

### **Describe the feature or solution you'd like to see implemented.**  
- **Core Functionality**:  
  - Detect and track lips movement in real-time using a camera feed or video input.  
  - Identify key points on the lips (e.g., corners, upper lip, lower lip).  
  - Tell about movement of lips
  
- **Output**:  
  - Provide output as speaking and not speaking
  
- **Deployment**:  
  - Make a seperate file for testing integrating all functions

---

### **Describe any alternative solutions or workarounds you’ve considered.**  
- **Alternatives**:  
  1. Using existing facial landmark detection libraries like MediaPipe or Dlib and customizing them for lip movement detection.  
  2. Leveraging pre-trained models for face and landmark detection (e.g., OpenCV + Deep Learning) and extracting lips-specific data.  

- **Challenges**:  
  - Existing models might not be optimized for precise and continuous lip movement tracking.  
  - Custom solutions could provide better accuracy but require more development time.  

---

### **Additional Context**  

- **Tech Stack Recommendation**:  
  - **Backend**: Model training and inference using TensorFlow or PyTorch Or you can use any of your choice.   
  -  Can use pretrained model

- **Additional Links/Resources**:  
  - [MediaPipe Face Mesh Documentation](https://google.github.io/mediapipe/solutions/face_mesh.html).  
  - [Dlib Python API](http://dlib.net/).

comment.body:
> T.b.h. I'm not really sure where this "67.67.67.67" network you were mentioning earlier even fits into the picture? You only need two networks:
> 
> * 10.0.0.1/30 - this is what your PC would see. This is where your "Esp" is the router. The "eth"
> * Some other network, couldn't care less what exactly, where you are a DHCP client and this network has internet access - this is what you get from the Wifi STA of the ESP and is possibly your home router network, which is "insecure" and where your PC should not connect (it connects to the 10.0.0.1/30 of the ESP)
> 
> That's it?

Yeah that was merely an exemple i used to illustrate the problem, it has no basis in reality.

> @indexds
> 
> Hmmm
> 
> > "something" "netif" by calling its "tx()" method. And the other way around for rx. <== THIS is unclear and this is where I don't think any bridging would help... :(
> 
> Actually... I take my words back. I'm no longer sure this will not work with bridging... Why wouldn't it and maybe you are right? Bridging the wg_netif + eth perhaps does exactly what you want, as this way the wg_netif would see each packet that comes via the eth, and will be able to "inject" new packets to the eth, which is maybe exactly what you want? Speculating. Anyway, on to your question:

Should be what I want. I think. The http server on the side would still see the request anyway right? The request would just be duplicated and also sent to the bridge which would then drop it or do whatever, which we don't care about. (I think.)


> Btw you can do the above purely with Wifi, as the Esp can operate simultaneously in an AP+STA mode. No need for Eth or anything like that.

I need eth because i'm building an usb key, I have a schematic that converts usb to eth frames that are interpreted by the esp32.

> This is a very heavyweight way to avoid converting `netif` to `esp_netif_t` but why don't you use this code (or similar):
> 
> https://github.com/esp-rs/esp-idf-svc/blob/2968fa1c109477436548b37e8251fff43a0d0b8f/src/netif.rs#L970
> 
> You just need to create a regular `EspNetif`, then wrap it with this driver, then bridge the wrapped `EspNetif` with the `Eth`, and then via the driver (`EspNetifDriver`) you have `tx()` `rx()` methods, so that you can pull/push packets from/to the bridge?
> 
> This means you need to do adaptation of the LwIP Wireguard code, but at least this is solving the "netif"-to-"esp_netif_t" problem?

I'll look into it, thanks. My main gripe with the whole conversion thing was I don't want to have to go through the thousands of lines of wireguard C code I have in the lib to modify everything to be esp_netif_t. If there's a way to wrap it in the rust layer, i'm all for it, otherwise i'll bite the bullet.

So shouldn't the implementation go like this :- 

```python
lc = torch.log_softmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
lu = torch.log_softmax(next_token_logits_m3id, dim=-1)
cutoff = torch.log(torch.tensor(cd_beta)) 
max_values = torch.tensor(lc.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values.item())
second_term = ((1 - gamma_t) / gamma_t) * (lc - lu)
m3id_logits = lc + torch.where(max_values < cutoff, second_term, torch.zeros_like(second_term))
```

Can you please clarify?

## タスクやディスカッションのリンク
- #135 

## やったこと
- `oauth2`のアプリケーション構築 (`python3 manage.py startapp oauth2`)
- `oauth2/`で`OAuth2`と`FortyTwoTokens`のテーブルを作成
  - セキュリティの観点から 管理者サイトでレコードを追加、編集ないようにしました 
  - 管理者サイトでアクセストークンとリフレッシュトークンを非表示にしました
- `oauth2/views.py` シリアライズ後の`User`, `OAuth2`, `FortyTwoToken`の情報を`api/oauth2/callback/`のレスポンスを返すようにしました

## やらないこと
- `oauth2/serializers.py`でvalidateの詳細定義
- `callback`関数の例外処理、エラー処理
- テスト
 
## 動作確認

管理者サイトから確認(`https://localhost:8000/admin`)できますが、OAuth2.0に関連するテーブルは一部非表示にしているため、今回はDBで動作確認する方法を記載します。（DBの削除は管理者サイトからの方が簡単かもしれません。）

1. `make build-up`
2. ブラウザで`http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/oauth2/authorize`を表示
  - 200 のステータスコードと定義した値が表示されていればOK
3. `make exec-db`
4. `psql -U <DB_USER> -d <DB_NAME>` 
  - `<>`は`.env`で定義されてる値を入力してください
5. 各テーブルを操作するコマンド（おもに動作確認で使用するコマンドのみ記載）
  - 確認
    - `\dt`: 全部のテーブルの表示
    - `SELECT * FROM <TALBE>;`: テーブルの中身を表示
      - `SELECT * FROM oauth2;`
      - `SELECT * FROM forty_two_tokens;`
    - 削除
      -  `DELETE FROM <TABLE> WHERE <field=name>;` テーブルの特定の中身を削除
        -  `DELETE FROM oauth2 WHERE id=1; `
        - `DELETE FROM forty_two_tokens WHERE id=1; `

## 特にレビューをお願いしたい箇所
- 特にチェックをお願いしたいポイントを簡潔に記述する
- 動作確認
  - `User`と`OAuth2`, `OAuth2`と`FortyTwoTokens`が紐づいてるかどうか
  - `FortyTwoTokens`する前に`OAuth2`を削除するとエラーになるかどうか
- モデルのパラメータの定義について

以下は自動生成や今後、削除する予定なので確認程度で大丈夫です！
- `oauth2/migrations/**` / 自動生成ファイルのため
- `oauth2/serializers.py`の`UserSerializer` / 今後、`accounts`から`User`を取得するため
- `oauth2/views.py`の各テーブルの表示方法 / テーブルの関連性を確認する目的で作成したため

## その他

今回、`User`と`OAuth2`のテーブルの関係は1対1で実装したので、複数のOAuth2.0認証のサービスごとにアカウントが作成される想定です。

詳細: DB / Account(User, OAuth2, FortyTwoTokens) [^1] 
[^1]: https://www.notion.so/DB-Account-User-Player-Friend-Block-be283778f87b43e8b0e8f058861e812f

  • Pending commands no longer run when --max-processes is set and an interruption/kill signal is sent - #433, #452, #460 Before v9.0.0, pressing Ctrl+C when --max-processes is set meant that only those commands would receive it. Once these stopped, the pending commands would start, which in turn meant that another Ctrl+C press would be necessary to stop them, and so on. Similar situation applied to combining --max-processes with --kill-others/--kill-others-on-fail.

    Starting with v9.0.0, this no longer happens, as these flags and/or key presses send a signal to stop the running commands in addition to preventing new commands from running.

  • The concurrently and default exports are now the same - #399 It's reasonable to expect that import { concurrently } from 'concurrently' would work the same as import concurrently from 'concurrently', however this has not been the case. The former used to be an unconfigured version of concurrently, lacking all features that you'd get from the CLI, which was seen as a "footgun". Both are now the same function.

```python
lc = torch.log_softmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
lu = torch.log_softmax(next_token_logits_m3id, dim=-1)
cutoff = torch.log(torch.tensor(cd_beta)) 
max_values = torch.tensor(lc.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values.item())
second_term = ((1 - gamma_t) / gamma_t) * (lc - lu)
m3id_logits = lc + torch.where(max_values < cutoff, second_term, torch.zeros_like(second_term))
```
Can you please clarify?
